quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What must drivers do when entering a roundabout or traffic circle?

options.text: Always stop before entering.
Yield to drivers already in the roundabout or traffic circle.
Have the right-of-way if there is one lane.
Have the right-of-way if there are two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already in the roundabout or traffic circle.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout or traffic circle, you must let drivers already in the circle go first.

questions.question: How should you look for a gap in freeway traffic when driving on an entrance ramp?

options.text: Look only in the inside rearview mirror.
Look only in the side view mirror.
Look in both the rearview and side view mirrors.
Look in your mirrors and turn your head to look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in your mirrors and turn your head to look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to find a gap when entering the freeway.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light at a railroad crossing mean?

options.text: Stop. Do not go until the signals turn off.
Slow down and go if the tracks are clear.
Go slowly with caution.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop. Do not go until the signals turn off.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see a warning signal. Warning signals include flashing red lights, crossing gates, a person signaling, or a train's horn. Never go around a gate or ignore a signal.

questions.question: How much sleep should teenagers get each night to avoid driving while tired?

options.text: Seven hours
Six hours
Eight hours
Nine hours

questions.explanation: Teenagers who sleep less than eight hours per night are more likely to have a crash while driving.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt and check that all passengers do the same before starting the car.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal ahead of time, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water. It is more likely with low tire pressure, bad tread, or high speeds on wet roads.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on wet roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Slow down by five to ten miles per hour.
Stay close to the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by five to ten miles per hour.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, reduce your speed by five to ten miles per hour.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently use the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brakes to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement safely.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and slow down by gently pressing the brakes. When you are at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to get back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrived first.
The driver who arrived last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway ends.
A one-way street begins.
A one-way street ends.
A divided highway begins.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead is now a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: You reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and get through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way when two vehicles arrive at the same time. Let that vehicle pass first, then you may go.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are making a turn.
You have your emergency brake on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times when driving.

questions.question: When do you NOT have to stop for a school bus with red flashing lights and its stop arm extended?

options.text: You are on the opposite side of a divided highway.
You are behind the bus.
You see no children nearby.
You can safely pass on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on the opposite side of a divided highway.
questions.explanation: You only do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing lights and its stop arm extended if you are driving on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Continue driving when you think the children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with its stop signal on. Do not proceed until the stop arm is pulled back.
